title: Parametric Two-Sample Hypothesis Testing
description: Evaluation of differences in means between two groups using Student's t-test and Welch's t-test.
conditions: Comparison of continuous outcome between two independent or paired groups
Sample size N >= 30 per group or verified normality of residuals
recommended_methods: Welch's t-test (unequal variances assumed) as the default independent two-sample test
Student's two-sample t-test (only if equal variances strictly verified by Levene's test)
Paired t-test for repeated pre/post measurements on the exact same subjects
selection_rules: Always default to Welch's t-test over Student's t-test; it maintains nominal Type I error rates under unequal variances
If data is paired (e.g. pre-treatment vs post-treatment on patient i), use Paired t-test on differences
If sample size N < 20 and data violates normality (Shapiro-Wilk p < 0.05), switch to Mann-Whitney U test
limitations: T-tests test only central tendency differences, not distribution shape differences
High statistical power on massive datasets (N > 100,000) produces statistically significant p-values for meaningless effect sizes
